preconditions.description: Input constraints: n is the number of sets (1 ≤ n ≤ 10000), k is the rank (1 ≤ k ≤ 100).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= m for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split())
postconditions.description: All integers in the n sets are within the range [1, m], where m is the minimal possible value printed on the first line.
The output consists of exactly n + 1 lines: the first line is m, followed by n lines of four integers each.
Each of the n sets contains exactly four distinct integers.

postconditions.expression: all(set(line.split()) == set(line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: Each set contains four distinct integers (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(all(k == gcd(int(a), int(b)) for a in line.split() for b in line.split() if a != b) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: For every pair of distinct integers in each set, their gcd equals k.

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(x) not in set.union(*[set(line.split()) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:i-1]]) for x in line.split()) for i, line in enumerate(stdout.splitlines()[1:], 1))
postconditions.description: No integer is used in more than one set (all sets are disjoint).
The first line of the output is the minimal possible m.
